Required study establishes Dutch and English instruction.

core: Calculus, linear algebra, probability, differential equations, numerical methods and mathematical structures
Programming, discrete mathematics, algorithms, optimisation and scientific computation
Probability, statistics, data analysis and empirical mathematical models
adjacent: Mathematics for scientific questions through Earth, climate, resource and energy systems

alternatives.label: Applied mathematics, algorithms & stochastic data models
alternatives.concept: Develop calculus, linear algebra, numerical methods, probability and linear systems through programming, logic, algorithms, optimisation, statistical learning and empirical stochastic models. This is the strongest applied and computational response to the stated Mathematics interests; proof-heavy analysis, algebra, topology and mathematical research remain explicit gaps.
alternatives.labelReason: The schedule contains a sustained mathematical/computational spine and concrete algorithmic and stochastic applications, while the label avoids claiming the target programme’s proof-intensive pure-mathematics depth.
progression: The schedule contains 24 unique courses, PPD in year one and nine advanced courses. Every formal prerequisite occurs earlier and every course is available in its assigned Fall 2026 cohort semester. Programming precedes algorithms and autonomous decisions; Mathematical Methods precedes dependent mathematics, robotics and neural networks. Research Methods & Statistics precedes Econometrics, while Probability & Statistics and Statistics & Experimental Methods precede the final empirical modelling work.

alternatives.label: Mathematical modelling, Earth systems & scientific data
alternatives.concept: Use calculus, linear algebra, numerical methods, probability, differential/linear-system models, programming and scientific data analysis to study Earth systems, climate, water–mineral processes, resources and renewable-energy systems. This answers the explicit mathematics-for-science direction without presenting Earth science as full Mathematics equivalence.
alternatives.labelReason: Thirteen mathematical/computational courses form the method spine, while ten Earth, climate, resource and energy courses supply coherent scientific systems to model and analyse.
progression: The schedule contains 24 unique courses, PPD in year one and eight advanced courses. Every formal prerequisite occurs earlier and every course is available in its assigned Fall 2026 cohort semester. Sustainability Essentials I precedes II and all dependent resource courses. Mathematical Methods precedes later mathematics, robotics and neural-network courses. Environmental foundations precede advanced biogeochemistry, recovery, resources and energy work.
alternatives.distinctness: Ten courses / 75 EC differ from the closest programme. The Earth-systems route replaces economics, general research methods, optimisation, networks, advanced algorithms, human-data statistics, decision-making and reinforcement learning with sustainability foundations, Earth-system analysis, field/laboratory environmental science, climate, resources and energy technology.

candidates.label: Mathematics for Earth systems and scientific data

selection.assessment: Two complete related-fields programmes pass the evidence, coherence, content, distinctness and feasibility gates. The closest route integrates mathematical methods with logic, algorithms, optimisation, probability, statistics and data models. The second uses the explicit science-connection interests to organise a materially different Earth-system and scientific-data route. A third proof-intensive pure-mathematics direction cannot supply cumulative real analysis, abstract algebra, topology, measure theory, number theory, complex analysis, specialist proof seminars or an 18-EC mathematics research project. These omissions remain explicit rather than relabelling adjacent computational or Earth-science work as full Mathematics.

blocks: Both provide programming used to implement mathematical work; UCR is a general programming foundation.
Both develop logical and discrete mathematical reasoning; UCR emphasises formal logic, discrete structures and algorithm construction.
Both establish calculus for mathematical problem solving; UCR also introduces matrices, complex numbers and differential equations.
Both introduce statistical inference; UCR also emphasises general research design, experiments and surveys.
Both address optimisation; UCR focuses on search, constraint satisfaction and optimisation for AI problems.
Both directly study matrices, vector spaces and linear transformations.
Both develop numerical equation-solving, approximation and error/stability reasoning.
Both model systems with differential equations; UCR specialises in linear systems, transforms and state-space representations.
Both establish probability; UCR integrates probability distributions, inference and simulation.
Both address differential equations; UCR combines them with multivariable and complex calculus rather than reproducing the full external ODE course.
Both develop regression and statistical models; UCR applies them to economic data.
Pure-mathematics depth, project and open profile
UCR has no separate breadth course introducing multiple areas of university mathematics through discipline-specific proof and problem work.
Logic and linear algebra do not reproduce a first abstract-algebra course.
UCR calculus does not reproduce a cumulative proof-intensive Analysis 2 course.
UCR logic and optimisation courses do not reproduce the target’s dedicated combinatorics-and-optimisation component.
The genuine 6-EC free-choice space remains open and is not assigned an invented UCR identity.
UCR PPD and course presentations do not reproduce a dedicated mathematics seminar in proof communication.
The one scheduled UCR linear-algebra course is already aligned with Linear Algebra 1; the second external course remains visible.
UCR Advanced Calculus includes complex functions but does not reproduce a dedicated complex-analysis course.
UCR has no second abstract-algebra course.
UCR has no algebraic-geometry or algebraic-curves course.
Applied courses do not reproduce the target’s advanced applied/industrial mathematics seminar.
No scheduled UCR course is represented as the target’s 18-EC mathematics bachelor project; optional independent research is comparison-only.
The genuine 30-EC free-choice space remains open and is not assigned invented UCR course identities.

notes.text: Both UCR pathways provide substantial calculus, linear algebra, numerical methods, differential/linear-system models, probability, programming and data analysis. Neither reproduces Leiden Mathematics’ cumulative proof-intensive analysis, algebra, topology, measure theory, complex analysis or dedicated mathematics research formation.
